operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are CamelCase or snake_case with underscores (Affiliated_With, On_Call, Trained_In, DateUndergoes, PrepNurse); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Tiny DB: largest table Room=36 rows, Block=12, Trained_In=15; original_values sampling of 5 with replacement will heavily repeat.

DATETIME columns store TEXT in two formats: date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD' (Trained_In, Stay, Undergoes) and 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (Appointment, Prescribes, On_Call). Date fuzzer template must be inferred per column from first parsable element.
DATETIME declared type dispatches to 'Date|Number(int elements)' branch: first element '2008-01-01' is not int, so Date fuzzer; but StayStart '2008-05-01' likewise. No int-stored dates here.
BOOLEAN columns (PrimaryAffiliation, Registered, Unavailable) store integer 0/1, not text; Bool fuzzer emits True/False which sqlite stores as 1/0 — fine.

Composite FKs: Room(BlockFloor,BlockCode)->Block(BlockFloor,BlockCode) and On_Call(BlockFloor,BlockCode)->Block; pragma foreign_key_list reports them as two separate single-column FKs, so fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws each column independently and can produce non-matching pairs (upstream behaviour).

Composite PKs: Affiliated_With(Physician,Department), Trained_In(Physician,Treatment), Prescribes(Physician,Patient,Medication,Date), Block(BlockFloor,BlockCode), On_Call(5 cols), Undergoes(4 cols) — PK-duplicate dropping is essential; Date in Prescribes PK is a DATETIME text.

Nullable columns: Appointment.PrepNurse (null_rate 0.222), Prescribes.Appointment (0.333), Undergoes.AssistingNurse (0.0 but nullable). FK fill from empty parent yields NULLs; NOT NULL not enforced in Python so insert may fail and skip.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, all parent tables/columns exist.
Medication.Description has distinct=1 ('N/A'); Room.RoomType distinct=1 ('Single') — String fuzzer with 5 sampled originals will mostly reproduce these.
Physician.SSN, Nurse.SSN, Patient.SSN are INTEGER but semantically 9-digit IDs (111111111, 100000001); Number fuzzer will emit small ints, breaking joins on SSN-like equality.

Cost REAL samples are round (1500.0, 3750.0); Number float fuzzer perturbs by ±0.01/±0.02 and draws uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from '(a,b)' args — REAL has no args so scale default, likely huge range.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template inferred from first element, e.g. '%Y-%m-%d' for Trained_In/Stay/Undergoes, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' for Appointment/Prescribes/On_Call; range = [min,max] of parsed originals (narrow, ~2008), so fresh dates cluster in 2008.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs (EmployeeID, DepartmentID, Code, AppointmentID, StayID, RoomNumber): full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none -> default), so PKs become large random ints; FK children draw from parent's final values so joins hold.
Number fuzzer on SSN/InsuranceID (INTEGER, no args): random ints, not 9-digit; queries filtering SSN ranges or joining Physician.SSN=Nurse.SSN will see implausible values -> likely FN.

String fuzzer on Name/Position/Address/Phone/Dose/RoomType: 5 sampled originals + pool literals, p=0.2 fresh random over a-zA-Z0-9() with contamination; Phone '555-0256' pattern lost -> queries with LIKE '555%' or phone format -> FN.
Bool fuzzer on PrimaryAffiliation/Registered/Unavailable: p=0.2 fresh True/False else element; fine.
Composite FK Room->Block drawn column-wise independently: BlockFloor and BlockCode pairs may not exist in Block -> join Room-Block yields fewer rows than expected -> FP/FN on block queries.

Composite PK duplicate dropping (sample_fresh_primary_keys) on Prescribes(Physician,Patient,Medication,Date) with Date as text: many rows dropped, table may shrink to near-empty -> queries counting prescriptions -> FN.

Tiny parent tables (Physician=9, Nurse=3, Patient=4, Department=3, Procedures=7, Medication=5, Block=12) with FK draw-with-replacement: child tables (Appointment, Prescribes, Undergoes, On_Call, Stay) get heavy duplicate FK tuples, then PK dedup collapses them -> very small child tables -> aggregate/count queries -> FN.
Prescribes.Appointment nullable FK: drawn from Appointment's final values or NULL; if Appointment table shrinks, many NULLs -> queries joining Prescribes-Appointment -> FN.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE single-column constraints beyond PKs; drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.

Literal pool from train SQL will contain 'N/A', 'Single', room letters 'A','B','C', dose '5','10', dates '2008-...' — String/Date fuzzers will reuse these, helping some equality predicates but not range predicates.
